requirements.requirement: Rotate /var/log/inventory/app.log on a daily schedule on node1
requirements.summary: logrotate.d/inventory created with 'daily' directive and validated syntax; logrotate.timer confirmed enabled (and active post-restart) to drive the daily schedule.

requirements.requirement: Retain seven compressed rotations of the log
requirements.summary: Config specifies 'rotate 7' and 'compress'. A forced rotation directly demonstrated compression working: app.log.1.gz was created and its decompressed content matched the pre-rotation log data.

requirements.requirement: Application can continue writing to the log after rotation
requirements.summary: copytruncate strategy used (avoids requiring the writer to reopen the file). A write immediately after the forced rotation succeeded and landed in the fresh, truncated app.log, and a further post-reboot write also succeeded.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task — daily rotation, retention of 7 compressed rotations, and continued application writes post-rotation — are directly demonstrated via a forced rotation test that produced a compressed archive and confirmed subsequent writes landed in the fresh log file. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol is also fully and coherently demonstrated: pre-restart boot_id (cce73776...) matches the after_prepare snapshot, post-restart boot_id (f1eca501...) matches the after_executor snapshot, and post-restart verification confirms the logrotate config, compressed archive, and write capability all survived the reboot. No unnecessary mutations or hygiene concerns were found.
limitations: The daily schedule itself was not observed triggering rotation over a real 24-hour boundary; only a manually forced rotation was captured, which is standard and sufficient evidence for logrotate configuration validation but does not directly observe an unattended daily trigger.

Retention of exactly 7 rotations across 7 rotation cycles was not directly observed (only one forced rotation cycle occurred); the 'rotate 7' config parameter is taken as sufficient supporting evidence given the task's scope.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor's state-changing actions were all tied to the task or the required restart-evidence protocol: creating /etc/logrotate.d/inventory (task requirement), removing the stale /var/lib/logrotate/logrotate.status stub before a forced test rotation (a bounded, low-risk step needed to make the on-demand rotation test deterministic, with no lasting negative effect since logrotate recreated its own state file), running a forced rotation and follow-up writes for verification, and the mandated systemd reboot with pre/post verification. The after-executor lifecycle snapshot shows no new failed services, no damaged package state, and no unexpected listening sockets or residual files beyond expected per-boot systemd-private directories and /tmp/reboot.log from the reboot process itself. No unnecessary or unexplained mutations were identified.
